    <title>Statistical Mechanics of Learning on Product Wasserstein Manifolds</title>
    <updated>2026-08-02T18:29:34Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01434v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.01434v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>Normally the statistical mechanics of learning treats constraints on weight distributions as restrictions that shrink the space of possible solutions. Therefore, it reduces model capacity. In this paper we would like to take a contrary approach, which, however, is based on the earlier work on distribution-constrained perceptrons. Rather than treating a prescribed weight distribution as a mere restriction, we propose that it defines the intrinsic geometry upon which learning naturally unfolds. We formulate both deep neural networks and variational quantum circuits as gradient flows on a product of Wasserstein manifolds -- one classical Wasserstein space for each layer and one quantum Wasserstein space for the circuit parameters.
